Hi Emily / Acme team — Kim from Redwood Compliance. Thanks for the clear asks; below is a concise mapping and proposed language we can include in the DPA to keep acceptance on track. I’ve attached the SOC 2 extract again and a one-page Dedicated-scope summary.

Short answers / recommendation: 

1) Archival segmentation (hot vs cold) — options we can offer:
   a) EU-cold-only (recommended for Acme): Redwood will store cold-tier archived artifacts (backups, long-term KV snapshots, archived logs that include customer-identifiers) in EU-only storage endpoints. Hot-tier (runtime KV cache) will remain in the region where requests are served; for Acme we propose EU primary region to minimize cross-border flows.
   b) US-hosted + escrowed keys: Redwood can retain archives in US but encrypt with an Acme-managed KMS key (BYOK); exports/exports to EU require documented export controls and SLA addendum.

   Proposed DPA clause (draft): "For archived artifacts containing personal data or identifiers, Redwood will provide an EU-only cold storage option. Where EU-only cold storage is enabled, backups and long-term snapshots will be maintained in EU regions and are subject to Acme-controlled keying where BYOK is selected."

2) SOC 2 scope for Dedicated: 
   - Redwood’s SOC 2 report covers our control plane and hosted runtime. Dedicated deployments are supported under our Shared Responsibility model. Evidence we can provide for Dedicated: control mappings, infrastructure configuration snapshots, and SOC2-relevant logs (redacted where necessary).
   - If Acme requires an independent SOC 2 attestation that explicitly names Dedicated infrastructure, that requires an audit-level supplement and will add 3–4 weeks to the acceptance window.
   Proposed DPA addendum note: "Redwood will provide SOC 2 control mappings and evidence relevant to Dedicated deployments under the Shared Responsibility model. Customer may request an attestation supplement for Dedicated environments; such request will be scoped separately and may affect timelines."

3) Deletion semantics / anonymization: 
   - "Delete" = logical delete from active runtime and index; physical overwrite of cold-tier backups is scheduled per retention window.
   - We can commit to irreversible deletion of archived copies on a specified schedule (e.g., 90/180/365 days), or provide irreversible anonymization upon request for historical snapshots.

Next steps I suggest:
- Ben: attach the one-pager and DPA draft to the MAP and push a Working Session for Tue 5/23 or Wed 5/24 (30 min).
- Emily: confirm preferred archival option (EU-cold-only vs BYOK+US-hosted) and target retention windows.

If Acme confirms EU-cold-only + standard retention (90 days hot, 365 cold), we can keep the original commercial close week of 5/22. If Acme requests an attestation supplement for Dedicated, we’ll surface the 3–4 week extension.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
